summary: A 1918 Aermotor steel tower on Black Mountain above Lake George, staffed until 1988 and now fenced off as a police radio site; closure dates conflict.

facts.design: 35-ft Aermotor LS40 steel tower (1918), extended by 39 ft in 1988 to 80 ft total
facts.status_note: Standing, but fenced off and used for police radio equipment

access.note: Tower closed to the public and enclosed by fencing; the site itself is open

visit.trail_note: Summit reached on foot; the tower and its fenced compound are closed to visitors

facts.agency: New York State Department of Environmental Conservation

events.note: First lookout: wooden fire tower built by the Conservation Commission
Replaced by a 35-foot Aermotor LS40 steel tower
Lookout operations ended at the end of the 1988 fire season; Explorer says staffed until 1988
Reinforced and extended with a 39-ft section for state police communications, 80 ft total
Wikipedia: officially closed by the DEC in early 1989
Explorer: off limits to the public since 1990

corrections.why: NHLR says the tower is currently closed to the public, and Wikipedia says the tower is closed off to the public while the site is open.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says the tower was officially closed in 1988, when it was extended. Wikipedia says lookout operations ended after the 1988 season and the DEC officially closed it in early 1989. The Explorer says it has been off limits to the public since 1990. The story reports all three without choosing one.

sources.title: Lake George’s Black Mountain is a hike through layers of clouds

notes_for_editor: The brief dated the build to 1918. Sources show a wooden lookout in 1911 that the 1918 steel tower replaced, so both are listed. Three different closure years (1988, 1989, 1990) are reported as found; a DEC or NYS Archives record would settle them. NHLR says the tower is closed and fenced; do not encourage climbing. The NYS Archives has 1918 photos of fire observer William C. Noble at Black Mountain (digitalcollections.archives.nysed.gov), seen only in search results and not used. The andyarthur.org pages returned 403 and were not read. No NRHP listing was found. Revised on fact-check 2026-10-08: the 80-ft total is now reported with the caveat that 35 ft plus 39 ft is 74 ft, and the story does not resolve it; 'still stands' is now footnoted to the present-tense Wikipedia text; sentences reworded where they copied source wording.
